items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board 2019 Delhi
items.stem: For what value of k, which the following pair of linear equations have infinitely many solutions: 2x + 3y = 7 and (k + 1)x + (2k − 1)y = 4k + 1
items.answer: Here a₁/a₂ = 2/(k + 1), b₁/b₂ = 3/(2k − 1) and c₁/c₂ = −7/−(4k + 1) = 7/(4k + 1). For infinitely many solutions a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂. Taking a₁/a₂ = c₁/c₂ we have 2/(k + 1) = 7/(4k + 1) ⇒ 2(4k + 1) = 7(k + 1) ⇒ 8k + 2 = 7k + 7 ⇒ k = 5. Hence the value of k is 5, for which the given equations have infinitely many solutions.
items.ocr: MinerU pushed the two printed equations out of the stem and into the solution; restored to the stem from the PDF text layer.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board 2019 Delhi
items.stem: Find c if the system of equations cx + 3y + (3 − c) = 0; 12x + cy − c = 0 has infinitely many solutions?
items.answer: Here a₁/a₂ = c/12, b₁/b₂ = 3/c and c₁/c₂ = (3 − c)/(−c). For infinitely many solutions a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂. From a₁/a₂ = c₁/c₂: c/12 = (3 − c)/(−c) ⇒ −c² = 36 − 12c ⇒ c² − 12c + 36 = 0 ⇒ (c − 6)(c − 6) = 0 ⇒ c = 6. From b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂: 3/c = (3 − c)/(−c) ⇒ −3c = 3c − c² ⇒ c² − 6c = 0. Hence the value of c is 6, for which the given equations have infinitely many solutions.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board 2020 Delhi Standard
items.stem: Determine graphically the coordinates of the vertices of triangle, the equations of whose sides are given by 2y − x = 8, 5y − x = 14 and y − 2x = 1.
items.answer: Write L₁: x = 2y − 8, L₂: x = 5y − 14 and L₃: y = 1 + 2x, tabulate a few points for each and draw the three lines. Taken in pairs the lines meet at A(1, 3), B(2, 5) and C(−4, 2). Hence the coordinates of the vertices of triangle ABC are A(1, 3), B(2, 5) and C(−4, 2).

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 2015
items.stem: Determine graphically whether the following pair of linear equations: 3x − y = 7 and 2x + 5y + 1 = 0 has: (a) unique solution (b) infinitely many solutions or (c) no solution.
items.answer: Writing 3x − y − 7 = 0 we have a₁ = 3, b₁ = −1, c₁ = −7; and for 2x + 5y + 1 = 0, a₂ = 2, b₂ = 5, c₂ = 1. Now a₁/a₂ = 3/2 and b₁/b₂ = −1/5. Since 3/2 ≠ −1/5, a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂ and the given pair has a unique solution. Plotting y = 3x − 7 through (0, −7), (2, −1), (3, 2) and y = (−1 − 2x)/5 through (2, −1), (−3, 1), the two lines intersect at (2, −1). Hence x = 2 and y = −1, i.e. answer (a) unique solution.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 2015
items.stem: Aftab tells his daughter, '7 years ago, I was seven times as old as you were then. Also, 3 years from now, I shall be three times as old as you will be.' Represent this situation algebraically and graphically.
items.answer: Let Aftab's present age be x years and his daughter's age be y years. Seven years ago (x − 7) = 7(y − 7) ⇒ x − 7y = −42 ...(1). After 3 years (x + 3) = 3(y + 3) ⇒ x − 3y = 6 ...(2). Equations (1) and (2) represent the situation algebraically. For the graph, x − 7y = −42 passes through (0, 6), (7, 7), (14, 8) and x − 3y = 6 passes through (6, 0), (12, 2), (18, 4). The two lines intersect at (42, 12), so Aftab's age is 42 years and his daughter's age is 12 years.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 2016
items.stem: For Uttarakhand flood victims two sections A and B of class contributed Rs. 1,500. If the contribution of X-A was Rs. 100 less than that of X-B, find graphically the amounts contributed by both the sections.
items.answer: Let the amounts contributed by sections X-A and X-B be Rs x and Rs y. Then x + y = 1,500 ...(1) and y − x = 100 ...(2). From (1), y = 1500 − x gives (0, 1500), (700, 800), (1500, 0); from (2), y = 100 + x gives (0, 100), (700, 800). The two lines intersect at (700, 800). Hence X-A contributes Rs 700 and X-B contributes Rs 800.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 2015
items.stem: Solve graphically the pair of linear equations 3x − 4y + 3 = 0 and 3x + 4y − 21 = 0. Find the co-ordinates of the vertices of the triangular region formed by these lines and x-axis. Also, calculate the area of this triangle.
items.answer: From 3x − 4y + 3 = 0, y = (3x + 3)/4 gives (3, 3), (7, 6), (−1, 0); from 3x + 4y − 21 = 0, y = (21 − 3x)/4 gives (3, 3), (7, 0), (11, −2). (a) The two lines intersect at (3, 3), so x = 3 and y = 3. (b) The vertices of the triangular region formed with the x-axis are (3, 3), (−1, 0) and (7, 0). (c) Area of Δ = ½ × 8 × 3 = 12. Hence the area of the triangle is 12 sq unit.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 2013
items.stem: The cost of 2 kg of apples and 1 kg of grapes on a day was found to be Rs. 160. After a month, the cost of 4 kg of apples and 2 kg of grapes is Rs. 300. Represent the situations algebraically and geometrically.
items.answer: Let the cost of 1 kg of apples be Rs x and of 1 kg of grapes be Rs y. The given conditions give 2x + y = 160 ...(1) and 4x + 2y = 300 ...(2). From (1), y = 160 − 2x gives (50, 60), (45, 70); from (2), y = 150 − 2x gives (50, 50), (40, 70). Plotting these points gives two parallel lines, so the pair is inconsistent and the situation has no common solution.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 2013
items.stem: Draw the graphs of the equations x − y + 1 = 0 and 3x + 2y − 12 = 0. Determine the co-ordinates of the vertices of the triangle formed by these lines and the X-axis and shade the triangular region.
items.answer: From (1), y = x + 1 gives (0, 1), (4, 5), (2, 3); from (2), 2y = 12 − 3x gives (0, 6), (2, 3), (4, 0). The two lines intersect at D(2, 3), so x = 2 and y = 3 is the solution of the given pair. The line CD intersects the x-axis at E(4, 0) and the line AB intersects the x-axis at F(−1, 0). Hence the co-ordinates of the vertices of the triangle are D(2, 3), E(4, 0) and F(−1, 0).

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 2013, 2012
items.stem: Solve the following pair of linear equations graphically: x + 3y = 12, 2x − 3y = 12. Also shade the region bounded by the line 2x − 3y = 2 and both the co-ordinate axes.
items.answer: Taking x + 3y = 6 ⇒ y = (6 − x)/3 gives (3, 1), (6, 0), (0, 2), and 2x − 3y = 12 ⇒ y = (2x − 12)/3 gives (0, −4), (6, 0), (3, −2). The two lines intersect at B(6, 0), so x = 6 and y = 0. Again ΔOAB is the region bounded by the line 2x − 3y = 12 and both the co-ordinate axes.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 Delhi 2012
items.stem: Solve the following pair of linear equations graphically: x − y = 1, 2x + y = 8. Also find the co-ordinates of the points where the lines represented by the above equation intersect y-axis.
items.answer: x − y = 1 ⇒ y = x − 1 gives (2, 1), (3, 2), (−1, −2); 2x + y = 8 ⇒ y = 8 − 2x gives (2, 4), (4, 0), (0, 8). The two lines intersect at A(3, 2), so the solution is x = 3, y = 2. Again, x − y = 1 intersects the y-axis at (0, −1) and 2x + y = 8 intersects the y-axis at (0, 8).

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 OD 2012
items.stem: Draw the graph of the following equations: 2x − y = 1, x + 2y = 13. Find the solution of the equations from the graph and shade the triangular region formed by the lines and the y-axis.
items.answer: 2x − y = 1 ⇒ y = 2x − 1 gives (0, −1), (1, 1), (3, 5); x + 2y = 13 ⇒ y = (13 − x)/2 gives (1, 6), (3, 5), (5, 4). The two obtained lines intersect at A(3, 5). Hence x = 3 and y = 5, and ABC is the triangular shaded region formed by the obtained lines with the y-axis.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 2013
items.stem: Solve the following pair of equations graphically: 2x + 3y = 12, x − y − 1 = 0. Shade the region between the two lines represented by the above equations and the X-axis.
items.answer: 2x + 3y = 12 ⇒ y = (12 − 2x)/3 gives (0, 4), (6, 0), (3, 2); x − y = 1 ⇒ y = x − 1 gives (0, −1), (1, 0), (3, 2). The two lines intersect at (3, 2), hence x = 3 and y = 2. ΔABC is the region between the two lines represented by the given equations and the x-axis.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 2015
items.stem: Solve x + y = 5 and 2x − 3y = 4 by elimination method and the substitution method.
items.answer: By elimination method: multiplying (1) by 3 and adding (2), 3(x + y) + (2x − 3y) = 3 × 5 + 4 ⇒ 3x + 3y + 2x − 3y = 15 + 4 ⇒ 5x = 19 ⇒ x = 19/5. Substituting in (1), y = 5 − 19/5 = (25 − 19)/5 = 6/5. By substitution method: from (1), y = 5 − x; putting this in (2), 2x − 3(5 − x) = 4 ⇒ 2x − 15 + 3x = 4 ⇒ 5x = 19 ⇒ x = 19/5, and then y = 5 − 19/5 = 6/5. Hence x = 19/5 and y = 6/5 by both methods.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 2015
items.stem: For what values of a and b does the following pair of linear equations have infinite number of solution? 2x + 3y = 7, a(x + y) − b(x − y) = 3a + b − 2
items.answer: From 2x + 3y − 7 = 0, a₁ = 2, b₁ = 3, c₁ = −7. The second equation gives ax + ay − bx + by = 3a + b − 2, i.e. (a − b)x + (a + b)y − (3a + b − 2) = 0, so a₂ = a − b, b₂ = a + b, c₂ = −(3a + b − 2). For infinitely many solutions 2/(a − b) = 3/(a + b) = 7/(3a + b − 2). From 2/(a − b) = 7/(3a + b − 2): 2(3a + b − 2) = 7(a − b) ⇒ 6a + 2b − 4 = 7a − 7b ⇒ a − 9b = −4 ...(1). From 3/(a + b) = 7/(3a + b − 2): 9a + 3b − 6 = 7a + 7b ⇒ 2a − 4b = 6 ⇒ a − 2b = 3 ...(2). Subtracting (1) from (2), 7b = 7 ⇒ b = 1, and then a = 5. Hence a = 5 and b = 1.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 Delhi 2012
items.stem: Find the value of p and q for which the system of equations represent coincident lines 2x + 3y = 7, (p + q + 1)x + (p + 2q + 2)y = 4(p + q) + 1
items.answer: Comparing with ax + by + c = 0, a₁ = 2, b₁ = 3, c₁ = −7 and a₂ = p + q + 1, b₂ = p + 2q + 2, c₂ = −4(p + q) − 1. For coincident lines a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂, i.e. 2/(p + q + 1) = 3/(p + 2q + 2) = 7/(4(p + q) + 1). From 3/(p + 2q + 2) = 7/(4(p + q) + 1): 7p + 14q + 14 = 12p + 12q + 3 ⇒ 5p − 2q − 11 = 0 ...(1). From 2/(p + q + 1) = 7/(4(p + q) + 1): 8(p + q) + 2 = 7p + 7q + 7 ⇒ p + q − 5 = 0 ...(2). Multiplying (2) by 5 gives 5p + 5q − 25 = 0 ...(3); subtracting (1) from (3), 7q = 14 ⇒ q = 2, and then p = 3. Hence p = 3 and q = 2.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | WORD PROBLEMS | Board Term-1 2012
items.stem: In an election contested between A and B, A obtained votes equal to twice the no. of persons on the electoral roll who did not cast their votes and this later number was equal to twice his majority over B. If there were 1,8000 persons on the electoral roll. How many votes for B.
items.answer: Let x and y be the number of votes for A and B respectively. The number of persons who did not vote is 18000 − x − y. Then x = 2(18000 − x − y) ⇒ 3x + 2y = 36000 ...(1), and 18000 − x − y = 2(x − y) ⇒ 3x − y = 18000 ...(2). Subtracting (2) from (1), 3y = 18000 ⇒ y = 6000. Hence the votes for B are 6000.
items.ocr: The book itself prints the roll size as '1,8000' (confirmed in the PDF text layer) while its solution uses 18,000; the stem is kept exactly as printed.

items.stem: Sum of the ages of a father and the son is 40 years. If father's age is three times that of his son, then find their respective ages.
items.answer: Let the ages of the father and the son be x and y respectively. Then x + y = 40 ...(1) and x = 3y ...(2). Solving (1) and (2), 3y + y = 40 ⇒ y = 10 and x = 30. Their ages are 30 years and 10 years.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | WORD PROBLEMS | Board Term-1 2013
items.stem: Half the perimeter of a rectangular garden, whose length is 4 m more then its width, is 36 m. Find the dimensions of garden.
items.answer: Let the length of the garden be x m and its width be y m. Perimeter p = 2(x + y), and since half the perimeter is 36 m, x + y = 36 ...(1). Also x = y + 4 ⇒ x − y = 4 ...(2). Adding (1) and (2), 2x = 40 ⇒ x = 20. Subtracting (2) from (1), 2y = 32 ⇒ y = 16. Hence the length is 20 m and the width is 16 m.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | WORD PROBLEMS | Board Term-1 2016, 2015
items.stem: A part of monthly hostel charge is fixed and the remaining depends on the number of days one has taken food in the mess. When Swati takes food for 20 days, she has to pay Rs. 3,000 as hostel charges whereas Mansi who takes food for 25 days Rs. 3,500 as hostel charges. Find the fixed charges and the cost of food per day.
items.answer: Let the fixed charge be Rs x and the per day food cost be Rs y. Then x + 20y = 3000 ...(1) and x + 25y = 3500 ...(2). Subtracting (1) from (2), 5y = 500 ⇒ y = 100. Substituting in (1), x + 20(100) = 3000 ⇒ x = 1000. Hence the fixed charge and the cost of food per day are Rs 1,000 and Rs 100.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | WORD PROBLEMS | Board Term-1 2012
items.stem: The present age of the father is twice the sum of the ages of his 2 children. After 20 years, his age will be equal to the sum of the ages of his children. Find the age of the father.
items.answer: Let the sum of the ages of the 2 children be x and the age of the father be y years. Then y = 2x ⇒ 2x − y = 0 ...(1). After 20 years, 20 + y = x + 40 ⇒ x − y = −20 ...(2). Subtracting (2) from (1), x = 20, and from (1) y = 2x = 2 × 20 = 40. Hence the age of the father is 40 years.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | WORD PROBLEMS | Board 2020 SQP Standard
items.stem: In the figure, ABCDE is a pentagon with BE || CD and BC || DE. BC is perpendicular to CD. AB = 5 cm, AE = 5 cm, BE = 7 cm, BC = x − y and CD = x + y. If the perimeter of ABCDE is 27 cm. Find the value of x and y, given x, y ≠ 0.
items.answer: Since BE || CD, BC || DE and BC ⊥ CD, BCDE is a rectangle, so CD = BE ⇒ x + y = 7 ...(1). Also the perimeter of ABCDE is 27 cm, so AB + BC + CD + DE + AE = 27 ⇒ 5 + (x − y) + (x + y) + (x − y) + 5 = 27 ⇒ 3x − y = 17 ...(2). Adding (1) and (2), 4x = 24 ⇒ x = 6. Substituting x = 6 in (1), y = 7 − 6 = 1. Thus x = 6 and y = 1.

items.stem: In Figure, ABCD is a rectangle. Find the values of x and y.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | WORD PROBLEMS | Board Term-1 2017
items.stem: Seven times a two digit number is equal to four times the number obtained by reversing the order of its digits. If the difference of the digits is 3, determine the number.
items.answer: Let the ten's and unit digits be y and x respectively, so the number is 10y + x and the number with digits reversed is 10x + y. Then 7(10y + x) = 4(10x + y) ⇒ 70y + 7x = 40x + 4y ⇒ 70y − 4y = 40x − 7x ⇒ 66y = 33x ⇒ 2y = x ...(1). Also x − y = 3 ...(2). From (1) and (2), 2y − y = 3 ⇒ y = 3 and x = 6. Hence the number is 36.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | WORD PROBLEMS | Board Term-1 2015
items.stem: 4 chairs and 3 tables cost Rs 2100 and 5 chairs and 2 tables cost Rs 1750. Find the cost of one chair and one table separately.
items.answer: Let the cost of 1 chair be Rs x and of 1 table be Rs y. Then 4x + 3y = 2100 ...(1) and 5x + 2y = 1750 ...(2). Multiplying (1) by 2 and (2) by 3: 8x + 6y = 4200 ...(3) and 15x + 6y = 5250 ...(4). Subtracting (3) from (4), 7x = 1050 ⇒ x = 150. Substituting the value of x in (1), y = 500. Thus the cost of a chair and a table is Rs 150 and Rs 500 respectively.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | WORD PROBLEMS | Board Term-1 2015
items.stem: A chemist has one solution which is 50% acid and a second which is 25% acid. How much of each should be mixed to make 10 litre of 40% acid solution.
items.answer: Let x be the volume of the 50% acid solution and y the volume of the 25% solution. Total volume gives x + y = 10 ...(1), and the acid content gives (50/100)x + (25/100)y = (40/100) × 10 ⇒ 2x + y = 16 ...(2). Subtracting (1) from (2), x = 6. Substituting in (1), 6 + y = 10 ⇒ y = 4. Hence x = 6 litre and y = 4 litre.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | WORD PROBLEMS | Board 2020 OD Standard
items.stem: It can take 12 hours to fill a swimming pool using two pipes. If the pipe of larger diameter is used for four hours and the pipe of smaller diameter for 9 hours, only half of the pool can be filled. How long would it take for each pipe to fill the pool separately?
items.answer: Let x be the time taken to fill the pool by the larger diameter pipe and y the time taken by the smaller diameter pipe. Then 1/x + 1/y = 1/12 ...(1) and 4/x + 9/y = 1/2 ...(2). Multiplying (1) by 9 and subtracting from (2), 5/x = 9/12 − 1/2 = 1/4 ⇒ x = 20. Substituting the value of x in (1), 1/y = 1/12 − 1/20 = (5 − 3)/60 = 2/60 = 1/30 ⇒ y = 30. Hence the times taken by the larger and smaller diameter pipes are 20 hrs and 30 hrs respectively.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | WORD PROBLEMS | Board 2020 Delhi Standard
items.stem: A man can row a boat downstream 20 km in 2 hours and upstream 4 km in 2 hours. Find his speed of rowing in still water. Also find the speed of the stream.
items.answer: Let x be the speed of the boat in still water and y the speed of the stream, so the upstream relative speed is (x − y) and the downstream relative speed is (x + y). Then 20/(x + y) = 2 ⇒ x + y = 10 ...(1) and 4/(x − y) = 2 ⇒ x − y = 2 ...(2). Adding (1) and (2), 2x = 12 ⇒ x = 6 km/hr. Substituting in (1), 6 + y = 10 ⇒ y = 4 km/hr. Thus the speed of the boat in still water is 6 km/hr and the speed of the stream is 4 km/hr.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | WORD PROBLEMS | Board Term-1 Delhi 2012
items.stem: A train covered a certain distance at a uniform speed. If the train would have been 10 km/hr faster, it would have taken 2 hours less than the scheduled time. And, if the train were slower by 10 km/hr, it would have taken 3 hr more than the scheduled time. Find the distance covered by the train.
items.answer: Let the actual speed of the train be s and the actual time taken be t, so distance = st km. First condition: st = (s + 10)(t − 2) ⇒ st = st − 2s + 10t − 20 ⇒ 2s − 10t + 20 = 0 ⇒ s − 5t = −10 ...(1). Second condition: st = (s − 10)(t + 3) ⇒ st = st + 3s − 10t − 30 ⇒ 3s − 10t = 30 ...(2). Multiplying (1) by 3 and subtracting (2), 3(s − 5t) − (3s − 10t) = −30 − 30 ⇒ −5t = −60 ⇒ t = 12. Substituting in (1), s − 5 × 12 = −10 ⇒ s = −10 + 60 = 50. Hence the distance covered by the train = 50 × 12 = 600 km.
items.ocr: The book's own first sentence is defective in both MinerU and the PDF text layer: it prints 'If the train would have been 10 km/hr scheduled time.' The missing words 'faster, it would have taken 2 hours less than the' are restored from the worked solution, which uses st = (s + 10)(t − 2).

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | WORD PROBLEMS | Board Term-1 2012
items.stem: The ratio of incomes of two persons is 11:7 and the ratio of their expenditures is 9:5. If each of them manages to save Rs 400 per month, find their monthly incomes.
items.answer: Let the incomes of the two persons be 11x and 7x, and their expenditures be 9y and 5y. Then 11x − 9y = 400 ...(1) and 7x − 5y = 400 ...(2). Multiplying (1) by 5 and (2) by 9: 55x − 45y = 2000 ...(3) and 63x − 45y = 3600 ...(4). Subtracting the two, −8x = −1600 ⇒ x = 1600/8 = 200. Hence their monthly incomes are 11 × 200 = Rs 2,200 and 7 × 200 = Rs 1,400.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | WORD PROBLEMS | Board Term-1 2012
items.stem: A and B are two points 150 km apart on a highway. Two cars start A and B at the same time. If they move in the same direction they meet in 15 hours. But if they move in the opposite direction, they meet in 1 hours. Find their speeds.
items.answer: Let the speed of car I from A be x and of car II from B be y. Same direction: distance covered by car I = 150 + distance covered by car II ⇒ 15x = 150 + 15y ⇒ 15x − 15y = 150 ⇒ x − y = 10 ...(1). Opposite direction: distance covered by car I + distance covered by car II = 150 km ⇒ x + y = 150 ...(2). Adding (1) and (2), x = 80. Substituting x = 80 in (1), y = 70. Hence the speed of car I from A is 80 km/hr and of car II from B is 70 km/hr.
items.ocr: MinerU truncated the opposite-direction step to 'x + y' and dropped '= 150'; restored from the book's own values (x = 80, y = 70).

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | WORD PROBLEMS | Board Term-1 2012
items.stem: If 2 is subtracted from the numerator and 1 is added to the denominator, a fraction becomes 1/2, but when 4 is added to the numerator and 3 is subtracted from the denominator, it becomes 3/2. Find the fraction.
items.answer: Let the fraction be x/y. Then (x − 2)/(y + 1) = 1/2 ⇒ 2x − 4 = y + 1 ⇒ 2x − y = 5 ...(1), and (x + 4)/(y − 3) = 3/2 ⇒ 2x + 8 = 3y − 9 ⇒ 2x − 3y = −17 ...(2). Subtracting (2) from (1), 2y = 22 ⇒ y = 11. Substituting this value of y in (1), 2x − 11 = 5 ⇒ x = 8. Hence the fraction is 8/11.
items.ocr: MinerU rendered the '1' added to the denominator as a stray superscript; the PDF text layer confirms it is 1.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | WORD PROBLEMS | Board Term-1 2012
items.stem: If a bag containing red and white balls, half the number of white balls is equal to one-third the number of red balls. Thrice the total number of balls exceeds seven times the number of white balls by 6. How many balls of each colour does the bag contain?
items.answer: Let the number of red balls be x and of white balls be y. Then y/2 = x/3 ⇒ 2x − 3y = 0 ...(1), and 3(x + y) − 7y = 6 ⇒ 3x − 4y = 6 ...(2). Multiplying (1) by 3 and (2) by 2: 6x − 9y = 0 ...(3) and 6x − 8y = 12 ...(4). Subtracting (3) from (4), y = 12. Substituting y = 12 in (1), 2x = 36 ⇒ x = 18. Hence the number of red balls is 18 and the number of white balls is 12.

items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | WORD PROBLEMS | Board Term-1 Delhi 2012
items.stem: The area of a rectangle gets reduced by 9 square units, if its length is reduced by 5 units and the breadth is increased by 3 units. The area is increased by 67 square units if length is increased by 3 units and breadth is increased by 2 units. Find the perimeter of the rectangle.
items.answer: Let the length of the rectangle be x and its breadth be y, so its area is xy. First condition: (x − 5)(y + 3) = xy − 9 ⇒ 3x − 5y = 6 ...(1). Second condition: (x + 3)(y + 2) = xy + 67 ⇒ 2x + 3y = 61 ...(2). Multiplying (1) by 3 and (2) by 5 and adding, 9x − 15y = 18 and 10x + 15y = 305 give 19x = 323 ⇒ x = 323/19 = 17. Substituting this value of x in (1), 3(17) − 5y = 6 ⇒ 5y = 45 ⇒ y = 9. Hence the perimeter = 2(x + y) = 2(17 + 9) = 52 units.
items.ocr: Question 98 was missing from this section file and from the next one, which starts at 99; restored here. The book misprints its own second condition twice (both misprints confirmed in the PDF text layer): it writes '(x + 3)(y + 2) = xy − 67' although the stem says the area is INCREASED by 67, and it writes '2x + 5y = 61' although its very next line multiplies that equation by 5 to get 10x + 15y = 305. Corrected to xy + 67 and 2x + 3y = 61, which are what the book's own x = 17, y = 9 and perimeter 52 require.
